2027-02-20.title: Second Saturday of the Great Fast
2027-02-20.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
2027-02-20.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba).
2027-02-20.verse: Yet wisdom is vindicated by her deeds.
theo: Jesus looks at his generation and sees children playing in the bazaar. “It is like children sitting in the marketplaces and calling to one another, ‘We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we wailed, and you did not mourn.’” One group wants to play wedding, the other wants to play funeral, and nobody joins anybody. So it was with John and Jesus. “For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, ‘He has a demon’; the Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, ‘Look, a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’” John's fasting was too strict for them; Jesus' table fellowship was too free. The real problem was neither the fast nor the feast. It was a heart that had decided in advance not to respond to God, whatever music he played.

There is a lesson here for the Great Fast. The Church plays both tunes in her year. Now she sings the lament of the fast; at Easter she will play the flute of the Resurrection and call us to dance. Ecclesiastes says there is “a time to mourn, and a time to dance”. The danger is to be the child who does neither: who keeps the outward forms of the fast without sorrow for sin, and who will keep the Easter feast without joy in the Risen Lord. Many men in our parishes take a pledge during the Great Fast to give up alcohol and smoking, and their friends sometimes mock them for it; and when those same men come to the Easter table with joy, someone else will find fault. Jesus' answer is quiet and final: “Yet wisdom is vindicated by her deeds.” Do not argue with the mockers. Let the fruit of the fast speak.

Paul's letter deals with a painful situation in the Church of Corinth, where a member was living in open sexual sin and the community had done nothing. He clarifies an earlier instruction: he did not mean that Christians must avoid every immoral person in the world, “since you would then need to go out of the world.” He means the Church must not pretend that open and unrepented sin among her own members is normal. “For what have I to do with judging those outside? Is it not those who are inside that you are to judge? God will judge those outside.” This is not a licence for gossip or contempt. Earlier in the same chapter Paul says the aim is that the sinner's “spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord.” The Great Fast turns this word first towards ourselves: “But if we judged ourselves, we would not be judged.” Before we sit in judgment on the world outside, the Church, and each of us within it, must look honestly at our own house.
outline: Ask: when God calls, do I dance or mourn, or do I do neither?
A heart that has decided not to respond.
Point 2 · A time to mourn, a time to dance
The fast now, the feast at Easter.
Point 3 · Wisdom vindicated by her deeds
Let the fruit of the fast answer the mockers.
“Yet wisdom is vindicated by her deeds.”
live: Give up a harmful habit (1 Corinthians 5:11)
If you drink or smoke, give it up for the rest of the Great Fast, and give the money saved to a family in need.
When someone laughs at your fast or your faith this week, answer with a kind deed instead of an argument.
Before saying anything critical about another person or about the Church, ask what needs correcting in yourself.
2027-02-20.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you came to us in the fasting of John and in your own table shared with sinners, and many would not respond. Do not let our hearts be like children who will neither dance nor mourn. Give us true sorrow in this fast and true joy at Easter. Free us from every habit that enslaves us, teach us to judge ourselves before we judge others, and let our deeds show your wisdom. Glory to you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: Jesus was called a friend of tax collectors and sinners; at the Holy Qurbana that friend invites sinners to his table, and those who come with repentant hearts go away rejoicing.

quick: Some would neither dance nor mourn: the problem was the heart, not the music.
There is a time to fast and a time to feast; let us do each fully.
Judge yourself before you judge others; let your deeds show wisdom.
2027-02-20.action: Give up one harmful habit for the rest of the fast and give the saving to the poor.
2027-02-20.question: Am I responding to what God is asking of me in this season, or finding excuses?

family.explain: Jesus tells about children who would not join any game: not the happy wedding game, not the sad funeral game. Some people were like that with God. They found fault with John for fasting and with Jesus for eating with sinners. Jesus wants us to respond to God with our whole heart: sad for our sins now, and full of joy at Easter.
family.intention: We pray for families hurt by alcohol and other addictions.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there something we complain about instead of doing what God asks?”

illus: A fisherman in Chellanam took the Lenten pledge to give up drinking. His friends at the evening gathering laughed and said he had become a priest. When Easter came he bought new clothes for his children with the money he had saved and invited the same friends home for appam and stew. One of them, half embarrassed, said: now you are celebrating too much. His wife laughed and said: first you said he does not drink with you, now you say he eats too much with you. Then she served them a second helping.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, friend of sinners, we come to you with open hearts. Help us to respond to your call. Amen.
share: We played the flute for you, and you did not dance (Matthew 11:17). Where have I failed to respond to God's call?
Is it not those who are inside that you are to judge? (1 Corinthians 5:12). What in my own life needs honest judgment this Lent?
Wisdom is vindicated by her deeds (Matthew 11:19). What fruit should my fast bear?
pm.resp: Lord, give us hearts that respond to you.
interc: For the Church, that she may be holy within and patient with all.
For men and women struggling with alcohol and drug addiction, and for their families.
For those who mock faith, that they may come to know Christ.
For all who have taken a Lenten pledge, that they may persevere.
For our group, that our deeds may show the wisdom of God.
pm.close: Father, your wisdom is shown in the deeds of those who follow your Son. Give us sorrow for sin in this fast, joy in the Resurrection, and strength to persevere. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Jesus compares his generation to children in the marketplace calling to one another: we played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we wailed, and you did not mourn (Matthew 11:17). They would join no game at all.

John fasted, and they said he had a demon. Jesus ate with sinners, and they called him a glutton and a drunkard (Matthew 11:18–19). The problem was not the music. It was hearts that had decided not to respond to God.

The Church gives us a time to mourn and a time to dance. Now is the time of the fast; Easter will be the time of the feast. Let us keep both with our whole heart. And when people mock our fast, let us not argue. Wisdom is vindicated by her deeds (Matthew 11:19).

Saint Paul reminds us to judge those inside before those outside (1 Corinthians 5:12). This Lent, let us first look honestly at ourselves, give up what enslaves us, and let the fruit of our fast speak for us. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus told about children who would not play any game, happy or sad. Let us not be like that with God! Now we are sorry for our sins, and at Easter we will be very happy. What good deed will you do today?

intro: Theme: “Yet wisdom is vindicated by her deeds.”
Children who will neither dance nor mourn, the seasons of fast and feast, and the self-examination the Church asks of her members.

sub: A heart that will not respond.
q: a time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;
‘We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we wailed, and you did not mourn.’
points.apply: Keep the rest of this fast with real sorrow for sin, so that you may keep Easter with real joy.

q: Let us test and examine our ways, and return to the LORD.
But if we judged ourselves, we would not be judged.
points.apply: Make a careful examination of conscience this evening.

sub: Do not argue with the mockers.
q: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom, and the knowledge of the Holy One is insight.
Who is wise and understanding among you? Show by your good life that your works are done with gentleness born of wisdom.
points.apply: Answer mockery with a good deed this week.

concl: The problem is never God's music, but a heart that will not respond.
Judge yourself first, and let your deeds speak.
2027-02-20.resolve: Give up one enslaving habit until Easter, and make an honest examination of conscience tonight.
